title: Sawtooth surge recovery latency scratch
body:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for sawtooth/sinusoidal arrival pattern runs — trying to capture recovery dynamics after repeated short surges (15m period) and to correlate tail latency spikes with KV cache cold fractions and batching behavior.

High-level summary (tl;dr):
- Pattern: sawtooth (15m period): ramp 0->4x baseline over 5m, hold 2m, drop back in 3m, idle remainder. Ran for 6 hours.
- Baseline qps: 150 steady; surge peak qps: 600 (4x).
- Hardware: 8x A100-80GB backends, instance pool with autoscale threshold at 400 qps per pool.
- Model: open-llama-like 13B quantized int8, KV cache size tuned to retain recent prefix only.
- Key finding: repeated short surges produce cumulative KV eviction cycles that increase p99 by ~3-4x after 3rd surge when cache hit rate drops below ~38%. Warm cache runs keep p99 < 120ms; degraded runs hit p99=420-500ms.

Run config (notes):
- Run id: saw-03-2026-03-10-T13
- Arrival generator: internal loadgen (poisson with sawtooth envelope), 30s sampling resolution to capture bursts.
- Concurrency limit per worker: 64 inflight.
- Dynamic batching: enabled, max batch size 128, batch timeout 12ms.
- KV cache: per-tenant, LRU with soft TTL 20m, capacity configured for 6M token prefixes.
- Autoscale: add worker at pool qps > 420 sustained for >60s; remove if < 200 for 120s.

Raw observations (selected timestamps):
- 00:00 start (cold-ish): cache hit 12%, p50 45ms, p95 210ms, p99 480ms (initial warmup).
- 00:30 after second surge: cache hit 62%, p50 32ms, p95 95ms, p99 150ms (nice warm cache behavior).
- 01:20 after 4th surge: cache hit 36%, p50 40ms, p95 220ms, p99 470ms (big tail).
- 03:00 sustained oscillation: median ~35ms, p95 140-210ms, p99 bimodal (130ms and 450ms spikes correlated with eviction events).
- 05:45 final cool-down: cache hit 68%, p50 28ms, p95 82ms, p99 120ms.

Interpretation / hypotheses:
1) Short repeated surges cause working set churn: soft TTL (20m) + LRU not enough to keep hot prefixes when amplitude spikes are frequent. Evicted prefixes cause expensive KV restore/compute which shows up in p99.
2) Dynamic batching hides some cost at p50/p95 but p99 is dominated by cache-miss tail and occasional batch scheduling delays when queue is emptied then refilled (microburst batching penalty).
3) Autoscale adds capacity but the new workers start cold (empty caches). If autoscale triggers during surge, net effect can be worse: additional capacity increases throughput but worsens global cache hit fraction and temporarily increases p99.

Quick experiment variations to run next (prioritized):
- V1: Increase soft TTL to 40m (keep everything else). Hypothesis: higher hit rate, lower p99, but increased memory pressure.
- V2: Aggressive prewarm policy: when new worker spins up, prefetch top-100 prefixes for the tenant using lightweight background requests. Hypothesis: prewarm reduces p99 when autoscale triggers.
- V3: Reduce max batch timeout to 6ms to avoid long batch tail during rapid queue drain. Hypothesis: slightly worse throughput but lower p99 during surges.
- V4: Tune autoscale hysteresis: require 180s sustained >400 qps before adding capacity, so new workers less likely to be added for very short surges.

Micro notes / interesting artifacts:
- Trace sample at 01:22 (trace-id t-01-22-evict): shows 320ms spent in KV restore + re-serialization; host CPU saturates doing dequantize/serialize work — consider offloading or faster path.
- Observed several cases where a single large batch (size ~120) blocks small incoming low-latency requests for up to 18ms because of synchronous batching queue flush. Consider partial flush or high-priority lane.
- When cache hit <40% we saw a second mode in p99 histogram ~420-500ms that aligns with cache restore path.

Action items (me / team):
- (Tara) schedule V1 run (TTL=40m) tomorrow morning, 6hr window; collect full histograms and heatmaps.
- (Eli) prototype prewarm shim that issues background prefix poke on worker start; aim for a safe PoC by EOD Fri.
- (Maya) check memory use across pool when TTL=40m; estimate delta and potential OOM risk.
- (Team) postmortem checklist entry: treat autoscale-triggered cold workers as first-class incident vector for tail latency.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- Could we have a distributed soft-cache index so that new workers can ask a lightweight directory for top-N hot prefixes instead of fetching full KV? Might reduce restore cost.
- Also think about a fast-path for single-token completions so that short responses avoid heavy serialize/deserialize cycles.

Unresolved questions:
- What is the exact working set size for this tenant over 6 hours (tokens)? Need to extract prefix cardinality counts from KV logs.
- Does prewarming increase token duplication cost significantly (double-counting billing)? Need to coordinate with billing/eng-sre.

Appendix: tiny ascii timeline (periods show surge ramps as /\):
- 00:00 ___/\____/\____/\____/\____ (6 cycles)
- marker: cycles 3-4 correlated with worst p99s in this run.

End.
